e10fefebccb2.layout: tall portrait, man clutching head in visible distress fills right 60% of frame, product tube floats left mid, bold headline top-left, two stat callouts below product

e10fefebccb2.text_on_image: Did Stress Break You? | It does more damage than you think. | Triple Magnesium Complex reverses it all | 1000mg Magnesium | 8 Hour Slow-Release

af7ab1793cbd.layout: tall portrait, white tile grid background, ceramic plate with product bars center, two bar wrappers top-right, spoon with coffee beans top-left, ingredient scatter, headline top, claim strip bottom

af7ab1793cbd.text_on_image: Introducing | mocha millet | 100% clean · 12g protein · Tasty as hell
af7ab1793cbd.angle_render: new-launch -> clean editorial flat-lay on tile with scattered coffee beans and spoon positions the bar as an artisan food product, not a supplement; the '100% clean · 12g protein · Tasty as hell' claim strip at bottom delivers the functional punch only after the sensory appeal is established
af7ab1793cbd.notable: Treating a protein bar like artisan food (ceramic plate, coffee props, tile flat-lay) is the whole bet — it says 'this is something you'd want to eat' before the protein claim appears.

71ba9a218725.layout: portrait, dark chocolate-brown background, product bag center-left, glass of golden shake right, wooden board with turmeric/pista ingredients scattered foreground, large headline top, claim icons bottom strip

71ba9a218725.angle_render: what's-inside -> the headline names ONE surprising ingredient ('curcumin') as the hook rather than listing the whole formula; real turmeric root, powder, pistachios, and almonds physically surround the bag so the ingredients exist in the real world, not just on a label; underline on 'curcumin' + annotation arrow treats copy like a textbook callout
71ba9a218725.notable: Spotlighting one unusual ingredient ('curcumin') as the headline — not '24g protein' — differentiates from the commodity protein crowd and creates curiosity before the functional stats land.

4d4bc8c0d5a5.layout: square, single product bag centered on abstract light-blue blob/organic shape cutout against white background; no additional props or lifestyle elements

4d4bc8c0d5a5.text_on_image: Yoga Bar | PRO CLEAN | PLANT PROTEIN | CHOCOLATE FLAVOUR WITH MONK FRUIT

4d4bc8c0d5a5.notable: The organic blob cutout instead of a plain white or flat-color background gives a DPA just enough visual energy to stop the scroll without requiring any additional creative work.

e3e99504b3bd.layout: square, single product box centered and floating on a clean warm cream/ivory background with generous breathing room; no text overlay beyond what is printed on the box

e3e99504b3bd.text_on_image: BLUE TOKAI | EASY POUR | MIXED BAG | 100% INDIAN SPECIALTY COFFEE
e3e99504b3bd.angle_render: catalog-DPA pure pack-shot -> the box is beautifully illustrated with peacock/landscape motifs and the packaging design itself does all the creative storytelling; DPA drops it on a clean cream canvas so the pack's craft stands alone; trust signal is aesthetic, not claim-based
e3e99504b3bd.notable: When your packaging is premium enough, the DPA creative job is just 'don't get in the way' — clean background, centered, full box, let the design sell.

914923507b7b.layout: square, dark vignette background, person (torso only) holds three product boxes fanned out, branded mug displayed bottom center with arrow annotation, two-line headline top, 'FREE MUG' badge bottom-right on yellow strip

914923507b7b.palette: dark near-black vignette background + bright yellow accent (free-gift callout) + brand blue/brown/navy packs; high contrast, urgent deal palette
914923507b7b.text_on_image: PREMIX COFFEE COMBO | YOUR DAILY LATTE FIX + A FREE MUG | Mug made of coffee | FREE MUG
914923507b7b.angle_render: bundle+free-gift -> person fans out three flavored coffee boxes like a hand of cards, making variety legible instantly; the free mug sits in foreground with a handwritten arrow annotation calling out the novelty ('Mug made of coffee'), so the gift feels like a discovery, not just a promotional line
914923507b7b.notable: The handwritten arrow annotation pointing to the free gift mimics how you'd physically point something out to a friend — converts a promotional claim into a moment of personal discovery.

83f6aac9ad91.layout: tall portrait, extreme close-up on woman's face and hand holding branded ON shaker bottle, outdoor/poolside setting blurred behind, no text overlay on image
83f6aac9ad91.type_treatment: no text on the creative itself; branded shaker with 'OPTIMUM NUTRITION' and 'ON' logo does all the brand signaling; copy is entirely in the caption/body text of the post

83f6aac9ad91.angle_render: lifestyle celebrity/influencer -> close-up on a well-groomed female fitness influencer confidently holding the ON shaker toward camera in golden outdoor light; the 'clean / no drama' copy angle is embodied by the ad having literally no text overlay — the confidence and clarity of the image IS the claim
83f6aac9ad91.notable: A zero-text creative where the clean influencer holding the clean black bottle enacts the 'no drama' copy message — the visual restraint is itself the brand statement.

fb214213d36f.layout: tall portrait, UGC/skit style — man sitting on bed edge in normal home setting, motion blur on upper body, white rounded-rectangle text card top-left with hook text
fb214213d36f.type_treatment: platform-native caption card: rounded white rectangle, bold black sans 'POV: Living with brain fog' — identical to TikTok/Reels native text style; no branded design elements on the creative
fb214213d36f.palette: everyday Indian home interior: yellow curtains, white walls, dark door, red fabric on bed; deliberately unremarkable, maximum relatability
fb214213d36f.angle_render: PAS video hook -> the 'POV:' caption card with a man in distress (hunched, motion-blurred, fumbling) recreates the feeling of brain fog through camera shake and body language before any product appears; built as a native skit so the thumb-stopping moment is recognition not advertisement
fb214213d36f.notable: The 'POV:' UGC skit format makes the viewer the protagonist of the problem — you're not watching someone suffer, you're reliving your own experience — which is why the hook works at zero production cost.

53043d6fbc40.layout: tall portrait, UGC/skit style — fit man in white t-shirt walks through gym doorway, platform-native text card top-center with hook question
53043d6fbc40.type_treatment: platform-native rounded white rectangle, bold black sans 'Protein se bloating?' — exactly matches Reels native caption treatment; minimal design fingerprint
53043d6fbc40.palette: gym interior: dark grey/charcoal walls, recessed lighting, wood-panel door, white tee on subject; real gym location, not a set
53043d6fbc40.angle_render: PAS problem hook in Hindi-English -> caption card poses the audience's exact objection ('Protein se bloating?') while a fit gym guy walks through the door — the hook targets the bloating-fear barrier that stops people from buying protein, using vernacular Hinglish to signal in-group credibility
53043d6fbc40.notable: Asking the objection as the headline ('Protein se bloating?') in Hinglish pre-qualifies the audience and makes the viewer feel understood before any solution is offered — classic problem-aware hook for a skeptical Indian gym audience.

38168c7dacf5.notable: Building a full 3D world from the flavor itself (the can literally sits inside a sherbet universe) makes the product feel like an experience to enter, not a beverage to consume — maximum emotional amplification of the flavor name.

93274a9b53bd.angle_render: science+collab -> the Firecracker Popsicle ice pops stand upright beside the hydration pack so the nostalgic summer flavor is immediately recognizable; 'CLINICALLY PROVEN HYDRATION' stacked large below the collab logo makes the functional claim sound like a lab result, converting a fun flavor launch into a credibility statement
93274a9b53bd.notable: Leading with a recognizable collab partner (Popsicle Firecracker) to earn the emotional click, then dropping 'CLINICALLY PROVEN HYDRATION' to earn the rational buy — emotional bridge to functional proof in a single creative.

65e43c9e78d2.layout: portrait, vivid blue textured background, three product stick packs arranged in a fan/row center, large discount offer headline stacked top two-thirds of frame

65e43c9e78d2.text_on_image: LIQUID I.V. | SAVE 30% ON EVERY ORDER | WHEN YOU SUBSCRIBE
65e43c9e78d2.angle_render: subscription offer -> the discount ('SAVE 30%') is the headline in the biggest type on the creative, with 'WHEN YOU SUBSCRIBE' as the secondary condition below; three packs fanned out show flavor variety as a subscription benefit; blue background signals the brand world so no lifestyle context is needed
65e43c9e78d2.notable: Making the discount number ('30%') the dominant visual element in the largest type treats the subscription mechanic as a product feature, not a footnote — the math IS the hook.

3d0fb75aafb5.angle_render: new-launch with stat callouts -> the 'NEW PRODUCT ALERT' ticker mimics a news broadcast to signal urgency; three floating macro badges (15g/6g/1g) act as the purchase rationale, radiating from the packs like a spec sheet; hands hold the outer boxes to give the graphic composition human scale
3d0fb75aafb5.notable: The news-ticker 'NEW PRODUCT ALERT' banner borrows broadcast-media urgency conventions for a food product launch, which makes the creative feel like a live event rather than a static ad.

b4e12f25f174.layout: tall portrait, extreme wide-angle low-angle shot of a Target store exterior, Target bullseye logo prominent upper-right, no product shown, no text overlay
b4e12f25f174.type_treatment: no text on image; copy is entirely in the feed caption ('New at Target Nationwide.', '75 ingredients, one easy ritual'); the retailer logo and storefront IS the creative message
b4e12f25f174.palette: Target red doors/logo + sandy beige building facade + bright blue desert sky; photographic, warm Southwest US location
b4e12f25f174.angle_render: retail distribution launch -> no product shown at all — the ad IS the Target storefront at an aspirational low angle; the placement signal ('now at Target') carries more purchase-trigger power than any product shot for an audience that shops Target; availability becomes the hook
b4e12f25f174.notable: Showing the retailer instead of the product is a counterintuitive move that only works when mass retail availability is itself proof of legitimacy — AG1 at Target is the credibility claim, not the product.

d4ffce1910e1.layout: tall portrait, two hands hold up two Poppi cans toward camera against beach backdrop (sand, ocean, blue umbrella), natural sunlight, no text overlay on creative

d4ffce1910e1.angle_render: lifestyle UGC -> two friends each hold a different Poppi flavor toward camera at the beach in a 'cheers' composition; the act of holding them up together suggests social ritual and variety without any text; the beach setting does the 'summer treat' positioning work, and the '5g Sugar' on-pack badge is legible for the functional-buyer
d4ffce1910e1.notable: Two cans in the 'cheers' position at the beach communicates social occasion, variety, and summer identity in one gesture — zero copy, all behavior.

d93b98c54a70.notable: Staging the 'about to make it' moment (pouch over empty bowl, neon sign glowing) in a real kitchen makes a new product launch feel like a personal discovery rather than a brand announcement.

a005cf9dfdcf.text_on_image: FOOD DRINK JR. | Milk Mix for 2-6 Yr Olds! | Real food your child can drink. | Website exclusive

56da9e58a37d.notable: Leading with benefit icons then hard-cutting to a strikethrough price is a reliable combo-deal template for Indian supplement audiences — the gym backdrop provides aspiration without requiring a human model.

8751f6fab9c2.layout: portrait — dark blue gradient bg, offer price badge top-center, four ingredient callout pills in two rows mid-frame, two product tubs bottom-center, single-line tech claim below tubs

8751f6fab9c2.palette: deep navy-to-black gradient (brand), electric blue edge-light accents, yellow badge and callout text — all brand-color, no photographic warmth
8751f6fab9c2.text_on_image: Pre-Workout 200 Xtreme & Creatine CreAMP Combo | OFFER PRICE | ₹1398 ₹949 | FLAT 32% OFF | 200mg Caffeine | 2000mg Beta-Alanine | Micronised Form | Higher Absorption | Powered By MB Creabsorb
8751f6fab9c2.angle_render: offer + science -> strikethrough price badge at top anchors value, then four ingredient-spec pills (dosage numbers in bold) bridge from 'cheap' to 'serious formula' before the tubs appear — price and specs reinforce each other

88e909f325d0.layout: square — large bold headline two lines top half, product box left-center, hand holding filled cold-coffee glass right-center, two stat callouts bottom-right (15g / 2 shots)

88e909f325d0.text_on_image: TASTES LIKE COLD COFFEE | POWERS LIKE PROTEIN | 15g WHEY PROTEIN | 2 ESPRESSO SHOTS
88e909f325d0.angle_render: us-vs-them -> two-line contrast headline (white line = familiar taste, yellow line = unexpected benefit) visually codes the 'two products in one' idea before any stats appear; hand holding cold-coffee glass makes the familiar side real, the stat callouts deliver the protein-side proof
